sheets.name: Introduction SOP
rows: PLACEMENT READINESS PROGRAM  ·  STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE
Introduction — Structure, Points to Exclude & Do's / Don'ts
SECTION A — INTRODUCTION STRUCTURE  (Follow this Order)

State your full name clearly.
(Optional — skip if already introduced by the interviewer)
Mention degrees in reverse order — most recent qualification first.
Describe work history in reverse order — most recent role first.

This is the CORE of your introduction.
Describe what you actually did — tools used, pipelines built,
infrastructure managed, deployments handled, etc.

List relevant technical skills, tools & services.
Keep it concise — do not explain each skill.
SECTION B — POINTS TO EXCLUDE FROM INTRODUCTION
Personal interests are irrelevant in a professional introduction.
This is for HR rounds — never volunteer it in an intro.
Personal / family background has no place in a job introduction.
Goals are discussed only when specifically asked by the interviewer.
Keep the introduction strictly professional and role-focused.
SECTION C — DO'S & DON'TS FOR INTRODUCTION

✓  Use past tense or present continuous tense
(e.g., 'Managed CI/CD pipelines' / 'Managing deployments')
✗  Don't use phrases like 'I can...', 'I will...', 'I want to...'
✓  Keep introduction duration to a minimum of 5 minutes

✗  Don't explain what a technology is —
state what you did with it
✗  Don't use client names or project names
✓  Speak with clarity, confidence and good pace

✗  Don't divide responsibilities by technology
(e.g., 'For Jenkins I did… For Docker I did…')
⚡  KEY REMINDER:  Minimum 5 minutes introduction  ·  Always focus on WHAT YOU DID, not what the technology is  ·  Past tense or present continuous tense only  ·  No client / project names
Placement Readiness Program  |  CDEC  |  Confidential — Internal Use Only

if it is totally irrelevant to the role

(e.g., 'Managed CI/CD pipelines')

✗  Don't explain what technologies are —
describe what you did with them

✓  Add ALL key skills — known and unknown
(tools, services, technologies)
✗  Don't use client names or project names

wherever available

(add marital status only if unmarried)

(e.g., 'For Jenkins I did… For Docker I did…')
